newsitem.title: JAPAN: NCB April debenture coupon seen unchanged-sources.
newsitem.headline: NCB April debenture coupon seen unchanged-sources.

text.p: Nippon Credit Bank Ltd (NCB) is likely to leave the coupon rate for its April five-year debenture unchanged at 2.35 percent, sources at long-term credit banks said on Tuesday.
The bank is also likely to leave its April long-term prime lending rate unchanged at a record low of 2.5 percent, they said.
NCB is expected to announce the coupon rate for its five-year debenture and its long-term prime rate for April on Wednesday.
The Industrial Bank of Japan Ltd (IBJ), the largest of Japan's three long-term credit banks, announced on Tuesday it would leave its long-term prime lending rate for April unchanged at 2.5 percent.
NCB last raised the coupon for its five-year debenture in February to 2.35 percent from 2.15 percent in January.

Despite the bank's announcement of a major restructuring plan on April 1, NCB debentures with a remaining life of one year or more are still being offered at a yield of around 7.0 percent, bond traders said.

No trades of NCB's new five-year debentures have been seen in the secondary market since mid-February, but its 4.5 percent five-year debenture maturing in July 1998 was traded at a yield of 7.0 percent on Tuesday.
